objective: First local test of dir:no_news_price_shock_reversal_chan (registry status: harvested, never backtested locally). Preregister 12 candidates (2 drop thresholds D in {5%,8%} x 3 hold horizons h in {1,3,5} sessions x 2 legs: long no-news drops (reversal) and short news-accompanied drops (drift, top-1000-ADV tier only, easy-to-borrow proxy, borrow cost modeled), all on close-to-close/next-open-fill calendar-time books comparable to S3) to resolve whether the Chan (2003)/Savor (2012) news-vs-no-news mechanism survives 2024-2026 costs and clears the owner's short-horizon-selective bar (high hit rate, high return per trade, few trades).
target_regime_and_horizon: TEST 2024-01-08..2026-09-17 is the anchor/decisive window per the brief. STRESS 2016-05-02..2023-09-15 is DATA-INFEASIBLE for this specific mechanism and is not computed as a decision window: the two PIT news sources used for classification (data/features/news_packets headline coverage, data/features/earnings_events 8-K item-2.02 filings) both have dense coverage starting only in 2024 (news_packets: 261/248/174 thousand rows in 2024/2025/2026 vs a combined 195 rows for all of 2011-2023; earnings_events/8-K: acceptance_utc range 2024-01-02..2026-09-17, zero rows before 2024). Classifying 2016-2023 drops as 'no-news' would mostly reflect missing data coverage, not an absence of news, and would bias the STRESS-window no-news leg upward (many real news days would be mislabeled no-news). This is checked and documented before any return is computed, per the data section's 'check coverage first, restrict windows to coverage' instruction; the brief's own 'TEST ... (anchor, decisive)' language makes this workable since TEST alone gates the decision.
existing_solution_comparison: `uv run oc research directions check` (both this session, and the 2026-09-29 intel pass I-20260929-01 section 2.2) confirms dir:no_news_price_shock_reversal_chan is registered with status=harvested and has never been locally backtested -- this iteration is the first local test, not a repeat. No local engine currently builds a dynamic-membership, event-triggered, capacity-capped (<=20 concurrent) calendar-time book on a rotating top-1500-ADV universe; the closest reusable infrastructure is scripts/screen_lane.py's frozen close-to-close/next-open-fill simulator (salvage.legs/salvage.simulate) and S3-comparison helpers (correlation_with_s3, diversifier_edge_for_offset, assert_same_session_convention, s3_incumbent), all reused unedited by this iteration's own scripts rather than reimplemented; screen_lane's own weights_fn/offset abstraction is built for a small fixed-universe periodic-rebalance rule and does not fit a rotating-universe event book, so this iteration writes its own weights-frame builder (scripts/run_h20260929_20_drop_reversal.py) that calls the same frozen salvage.simulate-equivalent P&L formula, extended (in this iteration's own code, not by editing salvage.py) to support per-symbol ADV-tier spread costs and a short-borrow carry cost, neither of which the frozen engine supports.
remaining_evidence_gap: Whether the no-news reversal leg or the news-drift (short) leg actually clears the brief's decision bar (calendar Sharpe >=1.19 OR S3 combo edge >=+0.05, trade-level edge over the shuffled-label placebo with t>=2, survives 2x costs) in the 2024-2026 US top-1500-ADV universe, given (a) Chan (2003)'s own robustness finding that the effect concentrates in small/illiquid names -- our cost tiering and ADV eligibility partly controls for this but does not guarantee survival, and (b) Dyl/Yuksel/Zaynutdinova (2019)'s decay finding that reversal/continuation magnitude shrank as liquidity improved post-decimalization, in a sample ending a decade before our window, with no post-2020 replication located -- meaning the current-era magnitude is genuinely unmeasured going in. This is exactly what the backtest computes, not assumed.
negative_experiments_checked: dir:end_of_day_reversal (already registered, a different mechanism: intraday last-30-minutes cross-sectional reversal, not headline-conditioned) and dir:letf_close_rebalancing_flow_reversal (refuted 2026-09-29, leveraged-ETF-flow mechanism, unrelated) are both distinct from this direction per the registry entry's own notes and are not reopened or duplicated here. dir:pead_xbrl_sue_filing_date and dir:pead_xbrl_8k_llm (post-earnings-announcement drift on SUE) are a related-but-distinct mechanism (drift conditioned on earnings surprise sign/magnitude, not on news-vs-no-news classification of a price drop) and were both evidence_too_weak locally; this iteration's short-news-drift leg is conceptually adjacent but conditions on the presence of any identifiable news/earnings event on a large-drop day, not on the sign or size of an earnings surprise, so it is not a rerun of the PEAD result.
cost_and_execution_assumptions: Signal at the close of day t (drop detected on a close-to-close, market[SPY]-adjusted basis); entry at the open of t+1; exit at the close of t+h for h in {1,3,5}; daily returns built close-to-close with next-open fills via the same P&L formula as the frozen S3 engine (salvage.legs/salvage.simulate), so correlation_with_s3/diversifier_edge_for_offset/assert_same_session_convention (screen_lane.py, reused unedited) are computed on a like-for-like convention, not the signal_card open-to-open convention the 2026-09-29 h20260929_12 session found understates correlation when mixed with S3's convention. Spread cost per side by ADV tier: top-500 3bp, 500-1000 6bp, 1000-1500 12bp, charged on turnover; 2x-cost variant also reported. Short leg (news-drift, top-1000-ADV tier only as an easy-to-borrow proxy) adds a 1%/year borrow fee accrued daily on the held short notional, on top of the tiered spread cost. Portfolio: equal-weight open positions capped at 20 concurrent and 10% of capital each, remainder in BIL; when more qualifying signals fire on one day than remaining capacity, the largest-drop-first, no-pyramiding-per-symbol tie-break is used (documented in candidate-manifest.json) -- a preregistered deterministic rule, not chosen after seeing results.
stop_condition: If, in TEST at base costs, no preregistered long no-news cell reaches calendar Sharpe >=1.19 or S3 combo edge >=+0.05 with a trade-level edge over the shuffled-label placebo (t>=2) surviving 2x costs, dir:no_news_price_shock_reversal_chan is refuted for this scope (US top-1500-ADV, 2024-2026, D in {5%,8%}, h in {1,3,5}) and not re-tuned on the same universe/window without a genuinely new signal (e.g. an intraday or options-flow feature this repo's daily-only data does not yet support). The short news-drift cells are reported the same way as separate candidates and do not gate the no-news leg's verdict or vice versa.

Savor 2012 "stock returns after major price shocks" news no news replication

no news price shock reversal strategy 2023 2024 2025 out of sample quant

sources.claim: Using a headline database to classify large individual-stock price moves as accompanied by identifiable public news or not: stocks with bad public news show significant negative drift for up to 12 months (slow reaction/underreaction); stocks with a large move and NO identifiable news tend to reverse the following month (overreaction to a non-fundamental move); both hold controlling for size/book-to-market; the no-news reversal is concentrated in smaller, more illiquid stocks and weakens (does not vanish) once low-priced stocks are excluded.
sources.applicability: Grounds the event definition and the expectation of an ADV-tier-concentrated effect.
sources.independent_replication: Corroborated by Savor (2012, different proxy) and Dyl/Yuksel/Zaynutdinova (2019, sample to 2015); no post-2020 replication found.

sources.claim: Using analyst-report activity as an information proxy around major one-day price shocks: shocks accompanied by information are followed by drift (continuation); shocks without information are followed by reversal; investors underreact to fundamental news and overreact to non-fundamental shocks; information-based changes correlate more with future earnings surprises; drift requires the price move and analyst-recommendation change to share sign.
sources.applicability: Second, methodologically distinct source behind the same mechanism; supports both the long no-news and short news-drift legs.
sources.limitations: Abstract-level only, SSRN/ScienceDirect both 403 on WebFetch.
sources.independent_replication: Same qualitative conclusion as Chan (2003) via a different identification method.

sources.claim: Independent replication of the Chan/Savor mechanism on extreme one-day price changes, sample 1986-2015: investors overreact to non-information-based price movements (reversal) and underreact to firm-specific public announcements (continuation/drift); effects concentrated in smaller firms and firms with lower institutional ownership, where the magnitude is also larger; liquidity improvement following the post-decimalization period reduced the magnitude of BOTH reversals and continuations -- a documented decay in effect size as market microstructure improved, over a sample ending a decade before this iteration's TEST window.
sources.applicability: The newest (2015-sample) independent replication located; its decay finding sets an honest prior against assuming Chan-era magnitudes hold in 2024-2026.
sources.limitations: Abstract-level synthesis via WebSearch only; ScienceDirect/SSRN both 403 on WebFetch; no post-2020 replication exists in located evidence.
sources.independent_replication: This IS the independent replication of Chan (2003)/Savor (2012).

cheapest_decisive_test.action: Build the event table from existing data only (data/features/universe_broad PIT ADV ranks, data/sip/daily prices, data/features/news_packets, data/features/earnings_events) and run all 12 preregistered candidates through a custom calendar-time book that reuses the frozen S3 close-to-close/next-open-fill P&L formula; check K1/K2/placebo/2x-cost survival directly -- no new data acquisition, no parameter search beyond the preregistered 2x3x2 grid.
cheapest_decisive_test.pass_condition: At least one long no-news cell reaches calendar Sharpe >=1.19 or S3 combo edge >=+0.05 in TEST at base cost, with trade-level average return per trade above the shuffled-label placebo (t>=2, clustered by date), surviving 2x costs.
cheapest_decisive_test.falsification_condition: No long no-news cell clears the bar above, or every apparent pass is beaten by its own shuffled-label or redated placebo.
